title: Unchecked Narrowing Integer Casts
pattern: Executing narrow casts (`as` conversions in Rust, implicit numeric narrowing in C++) on integer values specifying sizes or offsets derived from client-controlled packets.
why_bad: Narrowing casts discard significant bits. Casting `65537` to `u16` yields `1`. This causes the system to allocate a tiny buffer but then write large payloads into it, causing memory corruption or heap overflows in compiled binaries.
detection: Narrowing cast operators (e.g., `usize as u16` or `u64 as u32`) operating on data elements loaded from network or external stream lengths.
fix: Utilize safe, checked conversion traits (`try_into()` in Rust) that return errors if the value exceeds target bounds, rather than compiling silent truncations.
source: `Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)`, Ch 8; `Heather Adkins et al. (2020)`, Ch 12.
